This command compares two files and counts the number of lines that are different between them. The -U 0 flag tells diff to show only the differences, and the | pipe symbol sends the output of the first command to the input of the second command. The grep -v ^@ command removes any lines that start with an '@' character, which are added by diff when it shows the differences.

This command finds all files with a .txt extension in the /testbed directory, prints them to standard output, and then pipes them to xargs which processes them with wc -w to count the number of words in each file. The awk command calculates the average number of words per file by dividing the total number of words by the number of files minus one.
raw: find /testbed -name "*.txt" -exec cat {} + | xargs -I {} wc -w | awk '{sum+=$1; count++} END {print sum/count-1}'
command: find /testbed -name "*.txt" -exec cat {} + | xargs -I {} wc -w | awk '{sum+=$1; count++} END {print sum/count-1}'

Find all directories in /workspace, print them, and pipe the output to xargs with null delimiters. Then, pipe the output of xargs to du to get the size of each directory, sort the sizes numerically, take the two largest, cut the second column (the size), and pipe the output to xargs with {} as a placeholder for the directory path. Finally, pipe the output of xargs to du -sh to get the total size of the two largest directories in human-readable format.
raw: find /workspace -type d -print0 | xargs -0 du | sort -n | head -2 | cut -d" " -f2 | xargs -I{} du -sh {} | tail -1
command: find /workspace -type d -print0 | xargs -0 du | sort -n | head -2 | cut -d" " -f2 | xargs -I{} du -sh {} | tail -1
